role: Brand director B — recognition, distinctive behavior, and Nag attribution
reviewed: Previously inspected identity.png, poses.png, readme-390-day.png, and all-24.png

perClaimDecisions.reason: A wingless head can be strongly attributed to Nag without being named as a moth. My independent concern identified a plausible cue loss, not demonstrated confusion. Keep the current crop and anatomy. If human observations become available, record species naming and Nag attribution separately; neither result should silently stand in for the other.

perClaimDecisions.claim: Use the existing signature before replacing or narrowing it
perClaimDecisions.decision: accept correction and refine original concern
perClaimDecisions.reason: motion.js:98-110 already authors an antenna-first noticing sequence with a sharing glance; story.md names notice, get into it, share. The gap is demonstration and perceived effect in a particular context, not absence of an authored signature. Retain all 24 states, test existing curious behavior first, and treat repertoire emphasis as an application choice rather than deleting or replacing animation.

perClaimDecisions.claim: Comparable duration rather than identical timing
perClaimDecisions.reason: Exact elapsed-time matching would constrain the hesitation whose effect is being compared. Hold source content, scale, framing, destination, and observation conditions constant; use a comparable duration envelope and record actual durations and pacing. Evaluate whether the pause clarifies or delays the thought. No treatment should win merely because it receives substantially more viewing time.

perClaimDecisions.decision: agree with sequence and separate outcomes
perClaimDecisions.reason: Immediate identification of Nag, the project, and the useful observation comes first because unclear content cannot be repaired by a memorable character. Delayed avatar-to-Nag attribution answers a different long-term brand question and remains worth observing later. Passing one does not prove the other; exploratory responses are not population estimates.

perClaimDecisions.claim: Warmth leads and a gently wry contextual alternative merits comparison
perClaimDecisions.reason: The welcoming header is coherent and need not be replaced. Compare restrained personality variations around one verified project question without inventing an anecdote, failure, or accomplishment. A more overtly wry option is not automatically better.

acceptedPriority: Validate existing curious behavior with a source-checked project-question storyboard and still baseline, compare bounded investigation/share and restrained wry alternatives, then observe immediate comprehension and later attribution separately.
scopeStatement: I endorse the proposal unchanged as a priority-work and acceptance-criteria plan for the current foundation. This is not approval of unbuilt artwork, a release decision, or agreement to a score.
namedNonblockingLimits: My evidence remains still images and source inspection; temporal execution requires direct playback review when the experiment exists.
Human perception, attachment, recognition, and delayed recall remain unmeasured.
No calibrated numerical quality scale has been established; preserve current welcoming assets while testing alternatives.
scoreReason: My independent review assigned no numerical score. Pair agreement does not create measurement or justify a number.
